A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZeroFlow research. Their text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support comparison. v3 ends with references; v4 additionally contains readable Appendices A–B.

before.justification: v3 reports original accuracy, forgetting, memory, runtime, optimization-trajectory, and enhancement experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds combination ablations, replay evaluations, scalability measurements, longer task sequences, and optimization case studies.

M1.justification: Section 6 and Table 5 add an integrated variant combining hybrid FO/ZO training, historical gradients, and sparsification, which v3 evaluated separately. The constituent enhancements and seven forward-pass methods remain unchanged; Appendix A mainly documents existing procedures.

E1.justification: The four downstream datasets remain unchanged. The reported pretraining source changes from ImageNet-21K to ImageNet-1K, and Appendix B.3 adds replay-enabled MEMO evaluation beyond the previously evaluated setting that prohibited storing past examples.

E2.justification: Table 5 includes FO-SGD as an explicit reference alongside plain ZO-SGD for the enhancement comparison; the earlier historical-gradient and sparsity tables compared against plain ZO-SGD alone. The main benchmark retains its optimizer roster.

E3.justification: The main setup revises the stated pretrained initialization from ViT-B/16-IN21K to IN1K, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Added protocols include a 2,000-example replay buffer, batch sizes 64–512, larger ViT models, 20-task evaluation with FWT/BWT, and 100,000-step trajectory tests at learning rates 0.001 and 0.01.

E4.justification: v4 adds a joint-enhancement ablation (Table 5), memory sensitivity across batch sizes and incremental stages (Figure 9), local-minimum and learning-rate case studies (Figure 10), and longer-sequence robustness evaluation (Table 8). These substantially extend v3's separate enhancement and query-budget analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty across runs. v4's added random-seed discussion concerns regenerating perturbations for memory efficiency, not statistical replication.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values. New Table 5 reports combined-enhancement average/final accuracy of 62.07/51.94 versus 57.87/48.32 for plain ZO-SGD. Tables 6–8 and Figures 9–10 add replay, larger-model efficiency, transfer, memory-scaling, and failure-case results. These are additional results under their reported settings, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v3.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the synthetic old-task and new-task losses, and Equation 10 defines transfer quantities used in the added evaluation. No new theorems or proofs appear; the optimizer equations largely formalize procedures already described in v3.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the repeated claim of mitigating forgetting with just one forward pass with the narrower claim of using only forward passes. The benchmark novelty claim, seven-method scope, and three constituent enhancements are retained.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of enhancement complementarity and memory costs, plus specific qualifications concerning local-minimum trapping, conservative updates, and learning-rate-dependent convergence failures in Appendix B.2. The existing flatness, exploration, and from-scratch training discussion remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies optimizer formulas, Adam implementation clarification, exact synthetic losses, and initialization details. Section 4 documents layerwise perturbation regeneration and clarifies that a two-point estimate normally requires two forward propagations. Appendix B provides additional buffer, batch, learning-rate, step-budget, and GPU-capacity details. The explicit code-release timing promise is removed while the project URL remains.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for SPSA, stochastic three-point optimization, CAGrad, AMSGrad, and several continual-learning and foundation-model works, while removing the EWC and LoRA references. Its central positioning against gradient-dependent continual learning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, benchmark setup, and resource discussion receive localized rewrites, alongside terminology, affiliation, correspondence, and publication-header edits. Appendices A–B are added, but the main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Radar plots receive shared legends and revised styling; trajectories gain revised colors and minimum markers, and Figure 3 switches its illustrated optimizer pair. Existing figures are relocated, the query plot is enlarged, and Table 4 becomes full-width. Tables 5–8 and Figures 9–10 add substantial new displays.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies the misleading one-forward-pass claim and improves the paper's usefulness through explicit experimental definitions, broader validation, and concrete failure analyses. However, the unexplained ImageNet-21K-to-ImageNet-1K initialization revision accompanies unchanged main-table scores, leaving configuration traceability unresolved. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
